endorsements.quote: Governance plans should define degradation thresholds, authority to suspend the system, safe fallback workflows, user communication, retraining on non-AI pathways, and revalidation after major model, interface, or data-pipeline changes.

Governance plans should define degradation thresholds, authority to suspend the system, safe fallback workflows, user communication, retraining on non-AI pathways, and revalidation after major model, interface, or data-pipeline changes.
Override rates should be stratified by specialty, ward, seniority, and professional role where governance permits.

Metric specifications should include denominator, eligibility criteria, exposure definition, action definition, outcome window, data sources, linkage keys, confounders, risk adjustment, and audit rules.

For clinical governance, the framework supports proportional monitoring: high-stakes and high-involvement systems require stronger safety metrics, override analysis, de-implementation criteria, and fallback workflows.
De-implementation should be treated as a normal safety function rather than as a failure of innovation [ 17 , 18 ].
When AI-CDSS presents a top-ranked suggestion, differential diagnosis, or risk score, evaluation should consider anchoring and automation bias.
Where AI materially influences diagnostic reasoning, communication, triage, or documentation, governance should specify whether and how AI involvement is documented, disclosed, and explained.
Metrics should be integrated into monitoring dashboards, quality-improvement cycles, clinical governance committees, patient-safety processes, and de-implementation procedures.

unlisted_practices: Define an alert budget, such as expected alerts per clinician per shift, alerts per patient-day, and acceptable alert-to-action ratios, before deploying alerting systems.
Include educational-impact indicators, such as independent reasoning documentation, supervision patterns, and periodic non-AI case review, when AI-CDSS may influence training of junior clinicians.
Use a provenance policy for LLM prompts and outputs rather than universal full-content logging.
Do not use edit similarity as a standalone target for performance management or reimbursement, or as a clinical correctness or safety metric.
Consider outcome-linked procurement, reimbursement, or contracting only where endpoints are sufficiently attributable, auditable, and protected against gaming.
Map AI-CDSS metrics to existing hospital quality-management and patient-safety structures rather than creating a parallel measurement universe.
Label each outcome metric by proximity and attributability, treating distal endpoints such as mortality as weakly attributable without strong designs and risk adjustment.

screen.reason: This is a methodological and conceptual framework paper proposing governance, measurement, and deployment guardrails (such as DACS scoring, audit telemetry, and fallback workflows) for AI-CDSS, without analyzing new empirical patient data.
